## Correction — D39 was already documented, by me, earlier in this campaign

`conductor/docs/HONEST-LIMITS.md` carries a section headed **"The watchdog is a wall-clock
budget, and a local model spends it faster than a role needs"**, written in commit 91b1828,
earlier in this same campaign. It says:

> In the 14.2 probe the planner was killed by the watchdog on four occasions across three runs,
> twice in a single cell, costing thirty of that cell's sixty minutes — including once
> immediately after a *successful* decomposition, so this is not a recovery failure dressed up
> as a timeout.

That is D39. Same defect, same count, same "thirty of that cell's sixty minutes", with a
per-role rate table attached and an explicit statement that "a default sized for a cloud model
is not a default". **I recorded it, then re-derived it hours later and wrote it up as the
largest new finding of the campaign.**

**This is the third time in one session that the documentation held the answer and I did not
look**, after the Task 9.2 clustering defect and the `<placeholder>` semantics. The rule written
this morning — "a change to `planning.ts` clustering gets a mandatory grep of the finding
history for that function before the first line is written" — was scoped to one file, and the
failure it was meant to prevent recurred twice more outside that scope within the day. The
scoped version of the rule is not the rule. **Before recording any defect as new, grep
HONEST-LIMITS.md and the register for the mechanism, not the symptom.** The symptom here was
"planner sub-sessions die"; the mechanism was "watchdog", one word, one grep.

### What today's work actually added, stated honestly

Separating the re-derivation from the new contribution:

**Already known (HONEST-LIMITS.md, this campaign):** the kills, the count, the cost, the cause
at the level of "a sub-session is several requests and five turns of a role whose turns reach
451 seconds cannot fit in 900", and the operator consequence.

**New today:**

1. **Per-session emission accounting** (`scripts/gen_tokens.py --by-session`), which shows a
   killed session as large `reasoning` with zero `text` and localizes 86-92% of a cell's
   reasoning to planner sub-sessions. The earlier finding came from router ledger rows, which
   have no session identity.
2. **The reasoning CONTENT of the killed sessions** — the thing that produced an actionable
   change. One planner was writing complete test files (`plan.md`: "complete code, not a
   sketch"); another was deliberating over whether quoting `euler-cli-py`'s required
   `'<name> <answer> <milliseconds>ms'` would trip the no-placeholder rule. That reading is what
   D38's epoch-13 change is built on, and no ledger row could have produced it.
3. **D38 itself** — volume, 2.9x-25.7x baseline, ~90% reasoning — which is a different claim
   from D39's waste and is not in HONEST-LIMITS.md.

So the day's real yield is the instrument and the content reading, not the kill count. **The
kill count was a re-discovery, and the write-up that called it "the largest measured waste in
the campaign" was written by someone who had forgotten reading his own notes.**

### A retention gap, found by trying to check my own claim

I claimed the planner "is killed before emitting a single character". The earlier document's
mechanism — several turns summing past 900s — implies the session DID emit, as tool calls, and
the turn tables show killed planners making `bash` and `read` calls. **Those are not the same
mechanism and the difference is checkable**: a session with zero `text` but non-zero tool
arguments made calls and never returned a Plan; one with zero of both never emitted at all.

I could not check it. `run_and_watch.py` calls `clear_work_root()` at the start of every run, so
epoch 13's launch deleted every epoch-12 `opencode.db` — the only place the per-part record
lives. **The instrument built today reads inputs the harness destroys on the next run.**

Closed for epoch 13 onward: a snapshotter writes `<results>/generation/<cell>.generation.json`
(per-session reasoning / text / toolArgs / parts) as each cell's result lands, before the next
epoch can clear it. The JSON is small; the databases are not; and the question above is now
answerable next epoch rather than lost.

**D39's precise mechanism is therefore UNRESOLVED and must not be restated as settled** until
that check runs. What is certain is the kill count, the cost, and that the killed sessions were
doing coherent work when the deadline passed.

## The variance yardstick — and why epoch 13's primary prediction was a weak test

Two cells into epoch 13, the **baseline** arm supplied the number the campaign has been missing.
Baseline loads no packs, runs no plugin, and is untouched by every change made this session. It
is therefore a pure measurement of run-to-run variance:

| `baseline / slugify-ts` | generated tokens | reasoning share | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| epoch 12 | 6,364 | 82.9% | pass |
| epoch 13 | **614** | 45.2% | pass |

**A 10x swing on an identical arm and an identical task.** Nothing changed between them but the
sampling.

### What this invalidates immediately

`doctrine / slugify-ts` went 20,963 -> 16,049 tokens (-23%) and turned a 30-minute timeout into
a 22.9-minute pass. Read alone that is the epoch's headline. Read against the yardstick it is
**well inside the noise an unchanged arm produces**, and the timeout-to-pass flip is a crossing
of a threshold that sat 7 minutes away, which a 10x token swing clears trivially. The doctrine
arm did receive change #1 (the pack edit reaches it; `planPrompt` does not), so the result is
*consistent* with the change working. It is not evidence that it did.

Recorded before the rest of the epoch lands, so it cannot be quietly dropped if the remaining
cells look favourable.

### The pre-registered primary test is weaker than it was written to be

"Generated tokens fall on at least 3 of 4 conductor cells." Under a null where each cell is a
coin flip, **P(>= 3 of 4) = 0.3125** — the test fires by chance in roughly one epoch in three.
Against a per-cell variance of 10x, "fell" carries almost no information.

This is the multiple-comparisons trap from §5 wearing different clothes. The register already
records catching it once: a doctrine cell that looked monotonically decreasing across four
epochs, where the honest check ("1 of 7 cells with n>=3 is monotonic") said selection, and the
fifth sample returned to the original value. **The same arithmetic applies to a directional test
over four cells and I did not apply it when writing the prediction.**

### What the epoch can still support

The secondary predictions survive, because they are not continuous quantities subject to this
variance — they are **presence/absence of a specific reasoning behaviour**:

- **Secondary A** — placeholder deliberation. `doctrine / slugify-ts` epoch 13: **0 hits** over
  54,864 characters of reasoning. This is a fingerprint that is either there or not, and its
  epoch-12 appearance was verbatim and unmistakable.
- **Secondary B** — the decisions/options fingerprint, 101/55/68 in epoch 12, measurable per
  cell.
- **The watchdog-kill count**, 4 in epoch 12. A threshold crossing, not a magnitude.

**The token counts are demoted from primary evidence to context** until the campaign can afford
n>=3 per cell. Nothing about that is a surprise the protocol did not already warn about; the
surprise is that the yardstick was available every epoch, in the arm designed as a control, and
was never read as one.

### The instrument change this argues for

The bench runs `--reps 1`. Every cross-epoch token comparison in this register is n=1 against
n=1. **Baseline is the cheapest arm** — 0.7 to 7.7 predicted minutes against conductor's 22-40 —
so the marginal cost of running baseline at 3 reps is a few minutes per epoch and it buys a
measured noise floor for the epoch it is actually in, rather than a comparison against an epoch
run on different weights in a different thermal state. That is the next harness change, and
unlike the arm changes it cannot alter what it measures.


---

## The vacuous zero — a pre-registered fingerprint that confirmed itself by not running

`conductor / slugify-ts`, epoch 13, as the monitor reported it:

```
CELL conductor slugify-ts  TIMEOUT  30.0m  gen=11020 vs e12 18440 (-40%)
     | PH-fingerprint=0 DEC-fingerprint=0 | watchdog-kills-so-far=1
```

Tokens down 40%. Both pre-registered fingerprints at zero. Read straight, that is Secondary A
and Secondary B both landing on the first conductor cell of the epoch.

**It is vacuous.** The cell's five sessions:

```
mechanical:  10,348 reason   1,431 text
skeptic:      8,849 reason     700 text
<root>        7,251 reason     552 text
mechanical:   6,984 reason   1,541 text
skeptic:      3,976 reason     424 text
```

**No planner session exists.** The run never reached planning:

```
t+1193.1s  !! REFUSED conductor_classify: the skeptic sub-session produced no valid
              ClassificationCheck ({"kind":"env","reason":"watchdog timeout ... 900000ms"})
t+293.0s   << mechanical  dur=3m40s   ok
t+1193.1s  << skeptic     dur=15m00s  watchdog-timeout
t+1498.3s  << mechanical  dur=4m20s   ok
t+1642.3s  << skeptic     dur=2m24s   ok
```

The skeptic was killed at the watchdog during **classification**, the whole classify round was
re-run, and the 30-minute budget expired with the run still deciding what kind of work it was.
Both fingerprints live in the **planner** brief. Zero hits over zero planner reasoning is not a
measurement.

### This is D18 wearing a different hat

D18: `summarize_ledger_window` reported `partial` identically for an empty window, an unreadable
ledger, and rows without token fields — a metric that could not distinguish "measured nothing"
from "nothing to measure", and it turned seven passing tests into harness errors. The fix was a
`requests` count: a denominator, so an empty measurement announces itself.

**The same defect, in an instrument written today, by someone who had already fixed it once.**
A presence/absence fingerprint needs its denominator for exactly the D18 reason, and the monitor
now prints `over N planner-reasoning chars` or, when N is zero, `NO PLANNER RAN — both
fingerprints VOID`.

Worth stating plainly: **this one would have confirmed a pre-registered prediction.** The
epoch-12 register would have gained a row reading "Secondary A and B confirmed at n=1", and the
next reader — me, next week — would have had no way to see that the confirming cell never ran
the code under test. Pre-registration protects against choosing the test after seeing the data.
It does not protect against a test that cannot fail.

### The second finding, which is not about instruments

**The watchdog kill moved roles.** Epoch 12's four kills were all planners. This cell's kill is a
**skeptic, during classification** — a role and a phase D39 has never been observed in. Epoch 12
`conductor / slugify-ts` had zero kills and reached planning twice; epoch 13's has one kill and
reached planning never.

D39 is therefore not "the planner reasons too long for the watchdog". It is **"the watchdog is a
wall-clock budget and any role on this hardware can exhaust it"** — which is what
HONEST-LIMITS.md said in the first place, in a section headed "a local model spends it faster
than a role needs", generalising over roles rather than naming the planner. The narrower framing
was mine, from four samples that happened to share a role.

The effective rate for this cell is **6.1 tok/s** against epoch 12's 7.6-13.6 range, so the
40% token reduction bought nothing: it timed out anyway, from a different phase, at a lower
rate. Which is the variance yardstick's point restated — **at 10x per-cell noise, a 40% token
change is not a signal.**

## Epoch 13, first two columns — the token data is uninterpretable, as predicted

The variance-yardstick entry above was written when only `slugify-ts` had landed. `euler-cli-py`
completed it, and the result is cleaner than the argument was:

| arm | task | epoch 12 | epoch 13 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **baseline (control)** | slugify-ts | 6,364 | 614 | **-90%** |
| **baseline (control)** | euler-cli-py | 4,954 | 3,761 | **-24%** |
| doctrine | slugify-ts | 20,963 | 16,049 | -23% |
| doctrine | euler-cli-py | 8,178 | 11,811 | **+44%** |
| conductor | slugify-ts | 18,440 | 11,020 | -40% |

**The control arm's own spread, -90% to -24%, brackets every treated-arm decrease.** Doctrine's
-23% and conductor's -40% both sit inside the range produced by an arm that loads no packs, runs
no plugin, and cannot be reached by any change in this campaign. Doctrine then moved **+44%** on
`euler-cli-py` — the opposite direction from the same change on the same day.

Every arm moved both ways. The arm that moved most is the one nothing touched.

**Neither epoch-13 change can be evaluated on token counts.** That is not a disappointing
result; it is the correct reading, and the only reason it is available is that the control arm
was finally read as a control. The register has carried per-cell token deltas as evidence since
epoch 6. Every one of those readings was made against a noise floor nobody had measured.

### What survives, and what epoch 13 is now for

Wall clock and pass/fail carry the same variance and are demoted with the token counts. What
remains judgeable:

- **The fingerprints, when their denominator is non-zero.** Presence or absence of a specific
  reasoning behaviour is not a continuous quantity and does not scale with a 10x sampling swing.
  Two of four conductor cells remain.
- **The watchdog-kill count**, a threshold crossing. Epoch 12: 4, all planners. Epoch 13 so far:
  1, a skeptic during classification.

And the epoch's real yield is already banked and is not a measurement at all: the vacuous-zero
defect in the instrument, the role-generalisation of D39, and the calibration-reps change that
makes epoch 14 answerable. **An epoch that cannot decide its own pre-registered question can
still be the epoch that makes the next one decidable.**

### A standing correction to the register's own history

Every cross-epoch token or wall-clock comparison recorded before this entry was made without a
noise floor, at n=1 against n=1, with a control arm sitting unread in the same results
directory. Those readings are not withdrawn wholesale — some were large enough that a 10x floor
would not explain them, and the mechanical findings (D01, D09, D12, D18, D19, D20, D22, D23,
D31, D36) never depended on cross-epoch magnitudes at all. But **no cross-epoch magnitude in
this document should be cited as evidence without checking it against baseline's movement in
the same pair of epochs**, and where that check is not recorded, it was not done.

## `conductor / euler-cli-py`, epoch 13 — the first cell with a real denominator

```
CELL conductor euler-cli-py  TIMEOUT  45.0m  gen=17582 vs e12 26725 (-34%)
     | over 46,136 planner-reasoning chars: PH=17 DEC=2
     | watchdog-kills-so-far=2 (e12 total 4)
```

Secondary A predicted **zero** placeholder-deliberation hits. It got **17**. Read as written,
the prediction is falsified.

**It is the instrument that is wrong, and reading the hits says so in one line.** Three of the
four inspected are the model describing the task's own seed code:

> "The request replaces the **placeholder** main in src/cli.py with list/run commands..."
> "src/cli.py's main is a **placeholder** that prints 'not runnable yet' and returns 1..."

`euler-cli-py`'s seed `main` **is** a placeholder. The fingerprint `placeholder|strict checker`
matches an ordinary English word in a corpus where a stub function is literally called one. The
regex fires for a reason unrelated to the behaviour it was written to detect — **the third time
in one day** (D31's `\w{3,}` matching "the", the vacuous zero, this).

The fourth hit is the measurement the prediction was actually about:

> "...the task's own spec; the plan-writing doctrine says angle brackets quoting the task's
> spec are content, not a placeholder. **Fine for acceptance.**"

**The planner read the added sentence, applied it, and moved on inside a single clause.** The
epoch-12 planner facing the identical situation produced multi-paragraph deliberation and was
killed by the watchdog still deliberating. Same task, same rule, same model.

**Secondary A: confirmed in substance, falsified as written.** The hypothesis was right and the
metric was wrong, which is a better outcome than the reverse and is only visible because the
hits were read rather than counted.

### Secondary B — the one number this epoch can carry

`decisions`/options vocabulary, normalised per 1,000 planner-reasoning characters so it does not
inherit the 10x volume swing that made the token counts unreadable:

| | planner reasoning | DEC hits | rate per 1k |
|---|---|---|---|
| epoch 12 `euler-cli-py` | 90,353 chars | 50-55 (bounded: 55 cell-wide, planner is 92% of it) | 0.553 - 0.609 |
| epoch 13 `euler-cli-py` | 46,136 chars | 2 | **0.043** |

**A 13-14x reduction in rate.** A rate is not immune to sampling, but it does not move with total
volume the way a count does, and the epoch-12 figure is bounded from a measurement taken before
the change was designed.

This is the strongest evidence in the epoch, and it is still n=1. Two conductor cells remain.

### What did not move

**Watchdog kills are 2 at this point against epoch 12's 1** — slugify contributed a skeptic kill
epoch 13 where it had none in epoch 12. D39 is untouched by design and shows no sign of moving
on its own, which is the expected result and worth recording as a null rather than leaving as an
absence.

The cell still timed out, at 45 minutes, having generated 17,582 tokens. **Change #2 appears to
have removed a specific reasoning sink without changing the outcome** — the same shape as D36,
which cut planner reads >5x and changed no cell's result. That pattern now has two instances and
deserves to be named: *removing one named cost from a run that is 3-25x over budget moves the
budget, not the verdict.*

### The instrument fix this argues for

The PH fingerprint must match deliberation, not vocabulary. The distinguishing feature in the
epoch-12 text was **hedging around the rule's applicability** — "Careful:", "Hmm,", "but a strict
checker might", "to be safe" — clustered near the rule's own words, not the word "placeholder"
alone. Counting that is harder and more fragile than counting a noun, which is exactly why the
noun was chosen and exactly why it measured nothing. **A fingerprint for a reasoning BEHAVIOUR
cannot be a single content word that the task domain also uses.**


---

## The deliberation fingerprint, and Secondary A remeasured

`scripts/reasoning_fingerprints.py` replaces the word-count. The unit is **a hedge marker
occurring within 240 characters of a reference to one of the mechanical checks** — neither alone
scores. A model deciding whether a rule permits it hedges ("Careful:", "Hmm", "to be safe",
"a strict checker might") and hedges *near the rule's own words*. A model that has been told
what the rule matches on names it and proceeds.

The validation corpus is the two excerpts this register already recorded verbatim: what the
killed epoch-12 planner was thinking, and what the epoch-13 planner on the same task thought
after the change.

| excerpt | deliberations | rate/1k |
|---|---|---|
| epoch 12, killed mid-word | **5** | 8.33 |
| epoch 13, applied and moved on | **0** | 0.00 |

**Both texts contain the word "placeholder".** The fingerprint being replaced scored both and
therefore separated nothing; `test_reasoning_fingerprints.py` pins that failure so it cannot
return. It also pins the two halves of the rule: a rule reference with no hedge near it scores
nothing (naming a rule while complying with it is the *good* behaviour), and a hedge with no
rule reference near it scores nothing (ordinary uncertainty about the task is not deliberation
about a rule).

### The remeasurement

```
conductor / slugify-ts     NO PLANNER RAN — void
conductor / euler-cli-py   46,136 planner-reasoning chars   deliberations=0   rate/1k=0.000
```

**Zero across 46,136 characters**, from an instrument that scores 5 on a 588-character sample of
the prior behaviour on the same task.

**The honest limit on this claim:** it is not a rate-against-rate comparison. Epoch 12's full
planner reasoning is gone — `clear_work_root()` deleted it when epoch 13 launched, the retention
gap recorded above — so the "before" is a quoted excerpt, not a corpus. What can be said is that
the behaviour was present and verbatim in the epoch-12 planner that died, and is absent across
the whole of the epoch-13 planner on the same task. From epoch 14 the snapshotter makes this a
rate-against-rate comparison; for epoch 13 it is presence against absence, which is weaker and
is still the strongest form of evidence this epoch has produced.

**Secondary A: confirmed, on the second instrument.** The first instrument's failure and this
one's construction are both recorded because the difference between them is the whole lesson —
**a fingerprint for a reasoning behaviour cannot be a content word the task domain also uses**,
and the way to find out whether it can is to build a two-sample corpus of the states you mean to
separate before trusting the count.

## D40 — a checker's death throws away the thing it was checking

**Class:** harness. **Evidence:** n=1 cell, confirmed against the code. **Status:** open.

### What the cell did

`conductor / slugify-ts`, epoch 13, timed out at 30 minutes having implemented nothing. It never
reached planning. **80.6% of the cell's entire reasoning — 30,157 of 37,408 characters — went to
classification**, and the classification was never in doubt:

```
mechanical #1  3m40s  ok   -> kind "trivial"
   "A single, fully-specified behavioral change to one function in one file
    (src/slugify.ts) ... It maps to exactly one queue item"
skeptic    #1 15m00s  watchdog-timeout
   -> conductor_classify REFUSED
mechanical #2  4m20s  ok   -> kind "trivial"
   "A single, self-contained behavioral change to one function in one file ...
    no dependencies, and a one-liner stdlib implementation; it fits one queue
    item and needs no decomposition."
skeptic    #2  2m24s  ok
   -> budget expired
```

The classifier was right, twice, in nearly the same words. **The baseline arm completed the
whole task in 1.7 minutes** while conductor spent ~25 establishing that the task was small.

### The defect, in the code

`adapter/tools.ts::handleClassify` is one function that dispatches the classifier, then the
skeptic, and throws if either returns no valid value:

```ts
const skepticResult = await fanout.dispatch(skepticJob);
const check = skepticResult.value as ClassificationCheck | undefined;
if (check === undefined) {
  throw new Error("conductor_classify: the skeptic sub-session produced no valid ...");
}
```

The throw fails the whole tool call. The orchestrator's retry calls `conductor_classify` again,
which **re-dispatches the classifier from scratch**. A valid `Classification` — already derived,
already paid for at 3m40s — is discarded because a *different* sub-session, whose only job was
to check it, ran out of wall clock.

Mechanical #2 cost 4m20s to reproduce an answer the run was already holding.

### Why this is a harness defect and not another instance of D39

D39 is that the watchdog is a wall-clock budget too small for a role on this hardware. That is a
calibration mismatch and the honest fix is a number. **D40 is about retry granularity and is
wrong at any watchdog setting**: whatever the deadline is, some sub-session will occasionally
exceed it, and when the one that does is a *checker*, the checked artifact should survive. The
engine already declines to retry a watchdog abort internally (a deliberate choice — an abort is
not an env-flake), so the whole recovery path runs at tool-call granularity, which is the
coarsest available.

The two compound: D39 makes checker deaths frequent, D40 makes each one cost double.

### What it does NOT say

It does not say the skeptic is unnecessary. The skeptic exists to catch a classifier that
under-calls the work, and the register has no evidence about how often it does. **The claim is
only that its failure should cost its own re-run, not the classifier's.**

Nor does it say fixing this makes the cell pass. On this cell the saving is mechanical #2's
4m20s out of a 30-minute budget in which 15 minutes were already gone to the kill — the same
"moves the budget, not the verdict" shape that D36 and the epoch-13 doctrine change both had. It
is worth doing because discarded correct work is the cheapest kind of waste to stop, not because
it is expected to flip an outcome.


---

## `conductor / logfmt-lenses-ts`, epoch 13 — the counter-result

```
CELL conductor logfmt-lenses-ts  TIMEOUT  60.0m  gen=39857 vs e12 29755 (+34%)
     | over 129,022 planner chars: DELIB=4 (0.031/1k) DEC=0.667/1k PHword=19
     | watchdog-kills-so-far=4 (e12 total 4)
```

### Secondary B at n=2, compared against the right baseline

The monitor printed euler's epoch-12 range beside a logfmt cell, which is the wrong comparison
and would have flattered the result. Computed per task:

| task | epoch 12 planner DEC rate | epoch 13 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `euler-cli-py` | 0.553 - 0.609 /1k | 0.043 | **-93%** |
| `logfmt-lenses-ts` | 0.930 - 1.079 /1k | 0.667 | **-28% to -38%** |

Both fell. The magnitudes differ by more than 3x, and **there is no noise floor for this metric.**

That last point is a limitation of the calibration-reps change made earlier today, and worth
being explicit about: **the control arm cannot calibrate a conductor-only measurement.** Baseline
runs no planner, so extra baseline reps give a noise floor for tokens and wall clock and say
nothing about the variance of a planner-reasoning rate. Estimating that needs repeated
*conductor* cells, which are the most expensive in the corpus — 22 to 60 minutes each. The
honest position is that Secondary B is **directionally confirmed at n=2 and unquantified**.

### Secondary A at n=2, and the instrument's remaining over-match

DELIB=4 over 129,022 planner characters (0.031/1k). Reading all four: they are the model
**reciting the rule list to itself**, not deliberating over whether a rule applies —

> "avoid the literal words "TBD", "TODO:", ... **Be careful.**"
> "**Careful** about forbidden literal words in the markdown"

— and one of them shows the epoch-13 change being applied a second time, on a second task:

> "Also avoid the literal string `<placeholder>`. **Angle brackets quoting the spec are**
> [content]"

So the behaviour Secondary A predicted the absence of is absent again. But **the instrument
built four hours ago already over-matches**: "Be careful" as a self-reminder scores identically
to "Careful: [three paragraphs of uncertainty about whether this is allowed]". The hedge marker
is necessary and not sufficient; what distinguished epoch 12 was hedging that did not *resolve*
— an unresolved question carried across sentences. That is a harder thing to pattern-match and
the next version of this instrument has to try, because at 0.031/1k the current one is reporting
a number whose components mean two different things.

### The two numbers that matter more than either fingerprint

**Tokens moved +34% on this cell against -34% on `euler-cli-py` and -40% on `slugify-ts`, same
epoch, same changes.** Any account of epoch 13 that cites the token reductions has to explain
this one, and none can. The variance yardstick's verdict stands and is now demonstrated within
the treated arm rather than only in the control.

**Watchdog kills are 4 with one cell still to run, against epoch 12's 4 total.** D39 was left
untouched deliberately and the pre-registration said the count was expected to stay near 4. It
has. That is a null result on a threshold crossing, which is the one class of measurement this
epoch was designed to be able to make, and it says the epoch-13 changes did not reduce the rate
at which sub-sessions exhaust their deadline.

**Every conductor cell in epoch 13 has timed out.** 0/3 with one to run, against 0/4 in epoch 12.


### D40 — the fix is scoped, and deliberately not written tonight

`handleClassify` carries an unusually careful comment block, and it already contains the
argument that settles the fix:

> "The two dispatch refusals above are a different failure: a sub-session that returns no valid
> receipt has already spent the fan-out's own retry budget, **and its reply is not a function of
> the prompt**."

That is a good reason to re-roll the **skeptic**. It is not a reason to re-roll the
**classifier**, whose reply was valid, arrived in 3m40s, and said `trivial` — the same thing it
said again 4m20s later. The defect is that both are discarded together because the throw is the
only recovery granularity available.

**The natural slot exists.** `run.classification` is written provisionally at intake, and the
codebase already solves exactly this problem once, in a comment worth quoting because the fix
should copy it:

> "The field above is written provisionally at intake so run.json is a valid §2.3 record from
> the moment it exists, which makes its presence useless as the answer to 'has the run been
> classified?'"

...hence the separate `classified?: boolean` receipt. A second optional boolean —
"the classifier has spoken, the skeptic has not" — is the same idiom for the same reason.

**The obstacle is `trivialItem`.** Synthesis needs the classifier's proposed queue item, and
`run.classification` persists only `kind`, `rationale` and the skeptic `check`. Preserving the
classifier's work therefore means persisting a full queue item across a failed tool call and
answering whether a stored `trivialItem` is safe to synthesize from on a later invocation —
under a design whose stated posture is that an unconfigured or half-completed run "fails toward
conductor can do less, never conductor may do more".

That is a schema change with a safety question attached, and it is 02:40 with an epoch still
running and two arm changes from this epoch still only weakly evaluated. **Writing it now is how
D32 happened** — a fix applied to one of two call sites, breaking the invariant its own docstring
named. Recorded, scoped, and left for a session that can give it the review it needs.

**One alternative considered and rejected:** on skeptic failure, fall through and escalate to
`work` rather than throwing. It is cheap, needs no schema change, and fails safe in the design's
own direction. It is rejected because it makes the *common* case worse — every skeptic timeout
would push a correctly-trivial run onto the expensive path — to avoid a schema field. The
measured cell is `trivial` twice over; sending it to `work` on a timeout would have cost more
than the redundant classifier re-run it saves.

| conductor | 0/4 | **0/4** | 11,020 - 39,857 |

**Primary (tokens fall on >=3 of 4 conductor cells): NOT JUDGED.** Withdrawn before the data

**Secondary A (no deliberation about whether a spec quotation trips the placeholder rule):

```
euler-cli-py      DELIB=0 over 46,136 planner chars
logfmt-lenses-ts  DELIB=4 over 129,022  (0.031/1k — all four are the model reciting the
                                          rule list to itself, not deliberating)
clock-inject-py   DELIB=0 over 96,445

```

**Secondary B (the decisions/options fingerprint falls): CONFIRMED at n=3**, computed against
each task's own epoch-12 planner rate rather than the euler range the monitor was printing:

| task | epoch 12 /1k | epoch 13 /1k | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `euler-cli-py` | 0.562 - 0.609 | 0.043 | **-93%** |
| `clock-inject-py` | 0.581 - 0.825 | 0.394 | **-52% to -32%** |

### And the standing check, which is the result that matters

**Watchdog kills: 6, against epoch 12's 4.** Up 50%, and now present in **every** conductor cell:

```
conductor / slugify-ts        1     conductor / logfmt-lenses-ts  2
conductor / euler-cli-py      1     conductor / clock-inject-py   2
```

**Conductor: 0/4, for the eighth consecutive epoch.**

### The conclusion three epochs now support

This is the third confirmed instance of the same shape:

| change | what it moved | what it changed |
|---|---|---|
| D36 (source in the decompose brief) | planner read calls, 23-25 -> 4 | nothing |
| D38a (placeholder semantics stated) | deliberation, present -> absent | nothing |
| D38b (empty `decisions` stated legal) | options vocabulary, -28% to -93% | nothing |

**Removing a named cost from a run that is 5-18x over budget moves the budget, not the verdict.**
Epoch 13's conductor cells generated 5x, 4.7x, 15.7x and 17.7x their baseline counterparts. No
edit to a sentence closes a gap of that size, and the campaign has now spent five epochs
establishing that by doing it three times.

### What the measurement says to do instead

The `trivial` path exists to skip decomposition and planning entirely, and `slugify-ts`
**classified as trivial, correctly, twice** — while spending 80.6% of its reasoning on
classification and timing out having implemented nothing.

It did not fail because the path was wrong for it. It failed because the machinery that confirms
the path costs more than the path saves:

```
mechanical #1   3m40s  ok   -> "trivial"
skeptic    #1  15m00s  watchdog-timeout        <- D39
   -> conductor_classify REFUSED, classifier's valid result discarded   <- D40
mechanical #2   4m20s  ok   -> "trivial"
skeptic    #2   2m24s  ok
   -> 30-minute budget expired
```

Had the first skeptic returned in the 2m24s the second one took, classification would have cost
**~6 minutes**, leaving 24 for a one-file, one-function change that the baseline arm completed
in 1.7. **The trivial path is viable on this hardware and is being blocked by D39 and D40, not
by anything in the doctrine.**

That is the epoch-14 direction, and unlike the last three it is not a prompt edit: **D40 first**
(discarded correct work, wrong at any watchdog setting, schema change scoped above), **then D39**
(a wall-clock budget calibrated for hardware this is not). D39 second for the reason recorded
earlier — raising the watchdog lets long sub-sessions run to completion, which makes every cell
slower before any gets faster.

### The epoch's real yield

No scoreboard movement, and:

- **Four instrument defects**, each of which would have produced a confident wrong reading: the
  vacuous zero (a fingerprint that confirmed a prediction from a cell that never ran the code),
  the word-not-behaviour fingerprint, the wrong-baseline comparison, and rates having no noise
  floor at all.
- **The variance yardstick** — the control arm, sitting unread in the results directory for
  twelve epochs, moving 10x on a cell nothing touched.
- **D40**, identified, confirmed against the code, and scoped.
- **Calibration reps**, which make epoch 14 the first epoch able to measure its own noise.

An epoch that cannot answer its own question is still worth running if it makes the next one
answerable. That is now twice in a row, and it should be the last time: epoch 14's changes are
mechanical, its metric is a threshold crossing, and its noise floor arrives with it.

## D40 — fixed, and the fix is smaller than the one that was scoped

The scoped fix was persistence: store the classifier's `Classification` across the failed tool
call, which meant a schema change and a safety question about a stored `trivialItem`. **Re-reading
the epoch-13 evidence made all of that unnecessary.**

```
skeptic #1  15m00s  watchdog-timeout
skeptic #2   2m24s  ok            <- the SAME prompt, re-dispatched
```

A deadline exhaustion here is not deterministic. The retried round's skeptic settled in 2m24s,
which means the roll worth repeating is the one that failed — and the classifier's result is
still **in scope** at that point in `handleClassify`, so nothing has to be persisted at all.

`adapter/tools.ts` now loops the skeptic dispatch to `SKEPTIC_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS = 2` before
throwing. The throw is still the floor: two deadline exhaustions on the same check are no longer
plausibly a slow roll, and the phase gate's re-offer remains as the last recovery.

**Strictly better than the throw, by construction.** The throw path re-dispatches classifier *and*
skeptic; the in-place retry re-dispatches the skeptic alone. It does a subset of the same work.
Re-rolling the classifier has no value here — the run does not want a *different* classification,
it wants the one the check was about.

### The three guards this had to pass, none of which are the test suite

The fix is eleven lines. Landing it took three separate mechanisms saying no:

1. **`comment-hygiene` / the closed §7.4 vocabulary.** `journal.log(..., "skeptic-redispatch", ...)`
   failed `[vocab-callsites]`: adapters emit only names listed in `core/journal-events.ts`, and
   "widening the vocabulary means adding a name here (and a test that greps for it), never
   inventing one at the call site."
2. **The widening had to be argued, not asserted.** Every existing widening in that file carries
   a comment saying which existing name would have LIED. `fanout/retry` is the engine's own retry
   inside a single dispatch, emitted by the engine, so a handler-level re-roll filed under it
   becomes indistinguishable to a replay asking which layer recovered; `refusal` describes a call
   that failed and this one recovers; `guard-reject` names a verdict where no guard spoke. Hence
   `fsm/check.redispatched`.
3. **`[atlas-covers-every-journal-event]`.** A vocabulary name no atlas node claims is "a record
   no view can place", so the name needed a node explaining what seeing it means.

None of those is a test of the behaviour. All three are tests of whether the *observability* of
the behaviour is coherent, and they are the reason this codebase can answer "which layer
recovered" at all — which is exactly the question this campaign spent twelve epochs unable to ask
of its own runs.

**Verified red:** both new cases fail with `SKEPTIC_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS = 1`. The second pins the
bound (exactly two attempts, then refuse, receipt unset so the phase gate re-offers), because a
retry loop with no ceiling turns a recoverable stall into a hung round.

### Pre-registered for epoch 14

D40's saving is the redundant classifier re-run: **4m20s measured**, on a cell where 15 minutes
were already gone to the kill. So:

1. **A `check.redispatched` record appears** on any cell whose skeptic exhausts its deadline.
   This is the mechanical confirmation and n=1 suffices.
2. **`mechanical` sub-session dispatches per classify round fall to one**, where epoch 13's
   `slugify-ts` had two.
3. **NOT predicted: that any cell passes.** D39 is still untouched and is worth 15 minutes per
   kill, six kills last epoch. The register's own three-instance pattern says a named cost removed
   from a run 5-18x over budget moves the budget, not the verdict — and D40 is a smaller saving
   than any of the three that already failed to move it.

**The measurement that would change the strategy** is D39's: if the trivial path can complete
classification in ~6 minutes rather than ~25, `slugify-ts` has 24 minutes for a change the
baseline arm makes in 1.7, and the conductor arm has its first structurally plausible pass.

## D41 — the corpus shipped escaped prompts, and it took a request for a review page to find it

**Class:** corpus. **Evidence:** mechanical, the manifest itself. **Status:** fixed.

Asked to see the input prompts side by side with the outputs, the first thing rendering them
showed was that three of the four benchmarked tasks were never given the prompt their author
wrote. This is what `conductor / euler-cli-py` received, read straight out of the session store:

```
literal backslash-n: 6   real newlines: 0

"This package solves a collection of Project Euler problems through a solver registry. src/cli.py
exports main(argv) and does nothing useful. Make it the front end:\n- main([\"list\"]) prints every
registered solver name, one per line, sorted, and returns 0.\n- main([\"run\", NAME]) runs ...
```

A six-bullet requirement list, delivered as one line of visible escape sequences. The same held
for the seed `README.md` — three escapes, zero real line breaks — so the file the model opened to
orient itself was a single line.

**13 of the 23 tasks, 26 fields, every epoch, all three arms.**

### Why it survived thirteen epochs

Every channel that could have shown it hides it:

- **The manifest** is JSON, so `"...front end:\\n- main..."` looks correct in an editor. The
  double escape is the defect and it reads as the normal one.
- **`observed/*.turns.txt`** truncates the request at ~200 characters, before the first bullet.
- **The register** records what cells DID, never what they were asked. Twelve epochs of
  diagnosis, and the input was never once rendered.
- **The arms are affected equally**, so nothing in the scoreboard looks wrong. This is the part
  worth keeping: a defect that biases nothing produces no anomaly to chase, and the only way to
  find it is to look at the input directly — which no diagnostic question ever motivates.

### What it does and does not change

It does **not** invalidate the arm comparison. All three arms read the same corrupted text, so
every cross-arm claim in this register stands.

It does mean **three of the four tasks were harder than written**, for all arms, in every epoch.
`slugify-ts` is the one clean task, and it is also the one with the shortest prompt and no
bulleted list — so the correlation between "clean prompt" and "arms do best" is confounded by
size and should not be read as an effect.

### The fix, and the guard

The 26 fields are unescaped in `bench/conductor-tasks.json` (26 lines changed, no reformatting).

`conductor_bench.py::escaped_prose_fields` is checked by `load_manifest`, which now refuses the
corpus rather than running it. The rule is deliberately narrow: **only prose is checked** — the
prompt and any `README.md` — because a source file may legitimately hold those two characters
inside a string literal, and **a field carrying escapes BESIDE real line breaks is content, not a
defect**. `tools/run_tests.py` in seven tasks does exactly that and is correctly ignored.

Six tests, including one over the shipped manifest so a re-introduction fails in the suite rather
than in a run.


---

## D39 fixed — and the fix runs in both directions, which the pre-registration did not predict

The plan of record was "raise the watchdog". Measuring the roles first says that is half wrong.

Every `<< role ... dur=` line across epochs 12 and 13, 75 completed dispatches and 24 deaths:

| role | n ok | min | median | slowest ok | killed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mechanical | 25 | 1m38 | 3m29 | 6m10 | 3 (11%) |
| skeptic | 22 | 1m44 | **2m24** | 8m27 | 3 (12%) |
| planner | 28 | 3m54 | **7m48** | **13m38** | **18 (39%)** |

**The planner's slowest SUCCESS lands 82 seconds under the 900s ceiling.** A deadline that close
to the top of a role's successful range is not catching a pathology, it is cutting into the
normal distribution — and 39% of planners die on it.

**The skeptic's ceiling is six times its median.** A skeptic that is going to finish does so in
about two and a half minutes; one that is not costs twelve and a half before anything retries.
That is exactly what took `conductor / slugify-ts` in epoch 13: a dead skeptic at 15m00 in a
30-minute budget, on a task both classifiers called `trivial`.

**So one number cannot be right for both, and the correction is not monotonic.** Raise the
planner, lower the skeptic and the classifier. `parallel.roleTimeoutMs` overrides
`subSessionTimeoutMs` per role and falls back to it — deliberately the same shape as
`config.models.roles[role] ?? config.models.default` three lines away in the same function,
because the reason is the same.

```
mechanical  600000   (10m, against a 6m10 slowest success)
skeptic     600000   (10m, against 8m27)
planner    1200000   (20m, against 13m38)
everything else: the 900000 global, unchanged, because nothing measured it
```

Owned twice — `adapter/config-io.ts` and `scripts/conductor_wiring.py` — because
`conductor_bench.py` seeds a cell's config from the Python copy and **a seeded value overrides
the product default entirely**. A role tuned in TypeScript and not in Python would never reach a
benchmarked run. `composition.test.ts` reads the Python file and asserts the two maps equal, the
same guard the two existing shared constants already have.

### The structural finding underneath it

Two planner dispatches at the median — `decompose` then `plan` — is **15.6 minutes**, before a
line is implemented. At the slowest success it is 27. A T0 budget is 30.

**The `work` path cannot fit a T0 cell on this hardware.** Not "usually does not": the role's own
duration distribution excludes it. That makes the trivial path not an optimisation but the only
route, and reliable classification the whole game — which is what D40 and this change together
are aimed at.

### And a flake in the gate, found by running it

`test_etl_gate_times_the_frozen_baseline` failed at `speedup x1.95 is below the required x2.00`,
from runs of x1.68 and x2.34, while the baseline carried an injected 0.45s delay that puts the
true ratio well above 2. It set `GATE_TIMED_RUNS = 2` and asserted on the **median** — and with
two samples the median IS the mean, so one noisy run decides it.

Raised to 5, which strengthens the check rather than loosening it: the threshold is untouched and
the measurement of it is no longer a coin weighted by whatever else the machine is doing. Three
consecutive runs green, ~4 seconds added.

Worth recording where it sits: **a campaign whose central lesson is that n=1 wall-clock
comparisons cannot be trusted had a hard wall-clock threshold at n=2 inside its own gate.**
